subject: Dynamically sized types in user defined functions?

messages.author: 3d643362f888e7df
messages.subject: Dynamically sized types in user defined functions?
parts:
Hi

After reading through the manual on data types, declarations and user defined functions, I did not see how to provide a size at runtime, based on, say, an input argument.

My motivation is to use a system of ODEs whose size depends on the data.

Is this currently possible? If so how?

Thank you,
Marmaduke

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Dynamically sized types in user defined functions?
parts:
Hi!

So the number of equations can vary depending on data?

If so, then this should be doable in Stan, yes. System size of the ODE system is determined at runtime.

Sebastian

messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Re: Dynamically sized types in user defined functions?
parts:
(I'm doing a very similar task right now, trying to build a group-structured SEIR model, and want to be able to define the groups independently.)
If you need to do something a bit more complex, there is another trick that Bob Carpenter noted in a different thread;
If you have a real value, such as passing the value inside of the theta, you can do this;

    int k; 
    k <- 1; 
    while ((k + 1) < floor(p)) 
      k <- k + 1; 

Unfortunately, this can't then be used to define the size of a variable, it seems, since declarations must occur at the beginning of the UDF - unless someone has a trick for me to do this?
(I was thinking about calling another function to Jerry-rig the functionality I needed.)

Cheers,
David

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Dynamically sized types in user defined functions?
parts:
Two ways around that.

1. Put the sizing in a function and call it:

vector[my_size_function(a,b,c)] x;

2. Put it in a local variable:

int k;
k <- 1;

...
{
vector[k] x;
... use x ...
}
... can't use x ...

Usually these integer floor and ceiling functions are a bad idea,
which is why we haven't built them in. The exception is in interpolation,
where we'd like to have some built-in function support.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dynamically sized types in user defined functions?
parts:
No, it shouldn't be noticeable for performance.

Technically it's going to need to manage what's effectively
a new stack frame in the C++ for the scope of the nested variable
so that it can manage its destructor. But the destructor would
get called one way or another anyway, so it shouldn't be enough
of a performance hit to measure.

- Bob
